slides.title: What is Lock Out/Tag Out?
slides.description:
OSHA requires the use of locks, tags and other devices wherever maintenance or service is performed on equipment or machinery; e.g., lifts, bench grinders and air compressors

All service personnel should be familiar with LOTO program and when it applies to the maintenance of equipment

slides.title: Examples of LOTO procedures
slides.description:
A ballast in an overhead light needs to be replaced.

  • Throw the appropriate switch to “off” in circuit breaker box; close and lock the circuit breaker door box; place a tag on the box indicating who locked it out and why
  • Another option is to use individual lockout devices on the switch; tighten in place; add small lock or “icetongs”; place lock in one hole of device; add completed tag.

Bench grinder is defective and must be removed from service

  • Pull plug on bench grinder; place in plug-lock devise; add lock and complete tag.

In ground lift is not functioning properly

  • Lower lift to floor; bleed off air, place a bicycle lock on the air valve to keep it from being activated; add tag

slides.title: Hazardous energy forms covered by LOTO include:
When in doubt – lock it out!
slides.description: Just remember to make your shop safe by making sure that all employees are aware of any inoperative machinery, and that the tags are prominently displayed indicating that this item is unsafe to use

slides.title: The following items are required for an effective LOTO program:
slides.description:
• A written LOTO plan should be prepared
  • Reminder training
  • List of energy sources including electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, gravity, fluids and gases and mechanical
  • Must have an adequate supply of locks, tags, keys, hasps and chains
  • All energy sources must have hardware and tags
  • Electrical lines must be locked out or disconnected from power source during repair, servicing, adjusting, cleaning or set up/tear down
  • The shop manager or authorized personnel must have control of the keys
  • LOTO also applies to vehicles while being serviced (no keys in ignition during service)

PUT SAFETY FIRST BY USING THESE FEW GUIDELINES FOR EFFECTIVE LOCK OUT/TAG OUT PROCEDURES!

questions.question: What does OSHA require when maintenance or service is performed on equipment or machinery?

answers.b: Locks, tags, and other lockout devices

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of equipment that may require Lock-Out Tag-Out?
If a ballast in an overhead light needs to be replaced, what is the correct first step?

answers.b: Throw the appropriate switch to the “OFF” position in the circuit breaker box
answers.d: Leave the power on so you can test it

questions.question: Which energy forms are covered by Lock-Out Tag-Out?
A written L.O.T.O plan is required and should be documented in the OSHA manual in the dealership compliance dashboard for review.
